title.narrative: IRC HDP nexus i SRHR i Västafrika
IRC HDP nexus in SRHR in West Africa

description.narrative:
The programme is named Partnering for Resilience to Emergencies through Transformation of SRHR and aims to ensure that women and girls living in humanitarian and fragile settings in West Africa achieve their SRHR by leveraging sub-national and national gains for region-wide transformation. The projects three primary objectives are:
Objective 1: Strengthen the capacity of the weakest health systems to deliver rights-based SRHR services that are resilient in the face of conflict and disaster in fragile settings
Objective 2: Transform harmful social and gender norms that inhibit access to SRHR in fragile settings
Objective 3: Strengthen regional accountability for ensuring SRHR for women and girls in humanitarian and fragile settings

Detta programme har en regional ansats med en HDP nexus ansats och täcker fyra länder i Västafrika; Burkina Faso, Mali, Niger och Nigeria. Målgruppen är framförallt internflyktingar, flyktingar och andra personer drabbade av humanitära kriser då det geografiska valet av områden för implementering är områden drabbade av humanitära kriser och där en stor andel av befolkningen är internflyktingar och flyktingar. Kvinnor, flickor och ungdomar står i fokus.

This program has a regional approach with an HDP nexus approach and covers four countries in West Africa; Burkina Faso, Mali, Niger and Nigeria. The target group is primarily internally displaced persons, refugees and other people affected by humanitarian crises, as the geographical selection of areas for implementation are areas affected by humanitarian crises and where a large proportion of the population are internally displaced persons and refugees. Women, girls and young people are in focus.

sector.narrative: Basic Health Care Services in Emergencies

title.narrative: Signed Agreement IRC SRHR and Nexus in West Africa

description.narrative:
During the second year of project implementation, IRC demonstrates the following results:
Objective 1: Strengthen the capacity of the weakest health systems to deliver rights-based SRHR services that are resilient in the face of conflict and disaster in fragile settings
Nigeria: - A key achievement of Year 2 was the significant enhancement of frontline health worker competencies. From February 10 14 2025, three IRC-supported clinicians (one medical doctor and two nurses/midwives) completed an advanced Training of Trainers (ToT) course on Family Planning in Kenya. - The IRC successfully trained 115 health workers (110 women and 5 men) across the Northeast (12 17 May 2025 in Maiduguri; 20 May 01 June 2025 in Monguno (2 batches); 1 19 September 2025 in Adamawa (2 batches)) and Northwest (24th November 5th December 2025), significantly enhancing provider competence and confidence in delivering a broader range of contraceptive options. This directly translated into increased availability and uptake of voluntary family planning services in supported facilities. - Emergency preparedness was further reinforced through the development of Minimum Initial Service Package (MISP) response plans for Konduga and Monguno.
Burkina Faso: - A ten-day training on clinical family planning and postabortion care enhanced the skills of 41 health workers (6 men and 35 women) from the Fada district. In parallel, 2,000 hygienic delivery kits were distributed to 45 traditional birth attendants and to health centers across the three communes of Tibga, Diabo, and Diapangou, facilitating 1,244 safe deliveries in hard-to-reach areas. - Additionally, seventeen health facilities received essential medicines and consumables to improve obstetric and neonatal care. Awareness-raising activities reached 2,784 adolescents and youth (aged 14 to 25), including 1,002 girls and 730 boys among adolescents and 831 girls and 221 boys among youth, through conferences and informational sessions on sexual and reproductive health.
Niger: - From 24 to 28 February 2025, a training session on the Minimum Initial Service Package (MISP) brought together 22 participants (13 men and 9 women), including 20 frontline health providers, supported by two government trainers under the supervision of UNFPA and IRC. - The project identified and managed 55 cases of SGBV during the reporting period.
Mali: - IRC supported 4,069 antenatal consultations and 2,648 assisted deliveries. Stock-outs of certain contraceptive methods (pills, injectables, Implanon), observed between March and June 2025, were partially mitigated through enhanced coordination with UNFPA and dedicated logistical support. - A total of 249 community actors including 154 women and 95 men were trained on SRH, menstrual hygiene, and social mobilization approaches. Supported by quarterly incentive payments, they sensitized 4,678 individuals, including 3,467 women.
Objective 2: Transform harmful social and gender norms that inhibit access to SRHR in fragile settings Mali: - 50 community and religious leaders (31 men and 19 women) were trained in Mali from 27 to 30 August 2025, enabling them to conduct sensitization sessions that reached 1,578 people (1,234 men and 344 women) across six communes.
Burkina Faso: - In Burkina Faso, the Girl Shine model supported 50 adolescent girls aged 10 - 19 in Diapangou through six months of structured educational and recreational activities. Participants reported stronger self-confidence, awareness of trusted- person mechanisms, and the ability to assert themselves against violence, while safe-space enhancements improved psychosocial support for survivors. - Awareness and sensitization activities reached 4,154 individuals (2,426 women, 906 men, 505 boys and 317 girls) with key messages on the 72-hour reporting window for rape
Niger: - Between May and June 2025, eight facilitators (four women and four men) were trained to lead EMAP groups with 50 men, who completed 16 sessions on power dynamics, gender and GBV.
Objective 3: Strengthen regional accountability for ensuring SRHR for women and girls in humanitarian and fragile settings - In April 2025, IRC took a leading role in organizing the regional SRHR/GBV coordination meeting in Mopti, Mali, following the withdrawal of UNFPAs support - Beyond country-level coordination, IRC demonstrated strong regional influence by contributing to multiple high-level technical platforms across 2025. IRC played a leading role in: i) strengthening national SRH Working Groups within Health Clusters in Niger, Mali, and Burkina Faso, and, ii) co-leading the SRH Task Teams regional initiatives, including the rollout of SRH coordination tools and guidance in French. Engagement with WAHO and the Ouagadougou Partnership has been pivotal. Through technical contributions, coordination, and high-level participation, IRC helped reinforce: i) monitoring of SRHR commitments in humanitarian settings; ii) integration of humanitarian SRHR priorities into regional frameworks; iii) alignment of SRHR strategies across governments, UN agencies, and NGOs, and; iv) cross-country learning around MISP implementation and SRHR coordination.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
